title: Afternoon
description: A summer intersection in Kyoto, taken apart into what it is made of and lit again. Drag sideways to move the sun through the afternoon, from half past twelve to the last low light before half past six. The poles, the lamp standards and the buildings throw shadows that swing round and stretch across the road, the walls turn toward and away from the light, the cumulus warm on the faces the sun reaches, and the shadows of the clouds overhead drift slowly over the street and the hills. At the photographer's own sun it is the photograph.
intent: Reality pieces: depth maps and material maps, making a real place as real as possible but interactive. One photograph is baked into material maps (metric depth calibrated from the crosswalk and horizon, normals planar-fitted to the road and to walls read from the photo's own vanishing lines, albedo by dividing out the estimated sun and sky shading, the sun-shadow mask of the original light, a sky and cloud matte) and relit live: Lambert sun plus hemispheric sky, cast shadows by screen-space ray marching the depth toward a real solar position (Kyoto, 35 N, early August) plus exact capsule shadows for the hand-fitted poles and lamp standards and box shadows for the photographer's own corner just out of shot, sky and cumulus shaded from the same sun, cloud shadows projected through the photo's own cumulus, then developed through the shared film kit. Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrinsic_image_decomposition
sources: Photograph: street intersection in Japanese town (Kyoto, Sony a7 II) by Richard Tao (@richardtao28) on Unsplash, Unsplash License. https://unsplash.com/photos/street-intersection-in-japanese-town-jlJFU9QBfFc (file: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1583200786218-ccee132a8567). Cropped to 3:2 and resampled to 2400x1600. Depth by Depth Anything V2 (tools/depth/depth_hr.py), fitted to the ground plane's exact depth; maps baked by tools/depth/bakes/afternoon (prep.py, geo.py, orient.py, shade.py, light.json) into albedo.webp, normal.png (octahedral normal, occluder thickness), depth.png (16-bit log depth, the photo's sun-shadow mask) and matte.png (sky, cloud density, road).
